items.title: Will Iran withdraw from nuclear non-proliferation treaty?
items.desc: Iranian lawmakers have again raised the possibility of leaving a decades-old international nuclear weapons treaty. Analysts say the threat to quit may offer Tehran more leverage than an actual withdrawal.

items.title: Haiti ramps up the fight against gangs in the capital, but violence spreads elsewhere
items.desc: The killings in Kenscoff began late Sunday, when armed men descended on the farming community in the hills overlooking Haiti’s capital, setting homes ablaze and attacking residents. By Monday, bodies lay in the streets and survivors were searching for missing relatives.

items.title: One million children in Afghanistan face deadly malnutrition
items.desc: Some 3.7 million children in Afghanistan are suffering from wasting, one of the most dangerous forms of malnutrition, with around one million currently battling the most severe, life-threatening form of the condition.

items.title: As wars spread, the global food system unravels
items.desc: A family with four children abandoned its farm in Somalia after armed groups arrived and demanded payments for the right to continue cultivating the land. They walked roughly 100 kilometers to a displacement camp. One of the children died along the way.

items.title: Rohingyas in Myanmar suffering ‘heartbreaking’ misery and cruelty
items.desc: Members of the minority ethnic Rohingya Muslim group in Myanmar are “suffering, misery, and cruelty on multiple levels and across the country that is heartbreaking,” according to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

items.title: Land degradation is costing far more than restoring: UN deputy chief
items.desc: Countries are spending too little to restore degraded land even as the economic cost of doing nothing climbs towards $1 trillion a year, UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed warned at a major UN land conference in Mongolia.

items.title: Japan’s ‘2050 Weather Forecast’ highlights extreme heat in the future
items.desc: As extreme heat becomes an increasingly visible reality across Japan, meteorologists, scientists, businesses and professional footballers are joining forces to encourage stronger climate action and raise awareness of the risks posed by global warming.

items.title: UN chief, Red Cross renew call for rules on lethal autonomous weapons

items.desc: Among tent cities pitched on the rubble of destroyed homes in Gaza, children are, by one measure, finally getting enough to eat. By another, however, many of them may never fully recover, according to a new study by the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) released on Monday.

items.title: Two UN peacekeepers killed in South Sudan ambush
items.desc: Two UN peacekeepers have been killed and a total of seven people injured after unidentified gunmen ambushed a patrol in South Sudan’s eastern Jonglei state on Monday.

items.title: Security Council LIVE: Civilian suffering grows in Russia-Ukraine war
items.desc: As spiralling drone and missile attacks on civilians in the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war continue, top UN officials told the Security Council on Monday that every diplomatic effort must work towards a full, immediate and unconditional ceasefire. UN News app users can follow our live coverage here.

items.title: Global food supply has become ‘collateral damage’ in conflicts: Secretary-General
items.desc: The disruption of maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, Black Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait has worsened hunger crises and must immediately end, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said.

items.title: Security Council LIVE: War, hunger, flooding escalates in Sudan
items.desc: Suffering in Sudan continues to grow in the world’s worst humanitarian crisis amid brutal mass killings, abductions and rape, top UN officials warned the Security Council on Monday, calling for action to end the four-year-long war. UN News app users can follow our coverage here.

items.title: Sudan war: $22 million education boost to help 200,000 children
items.desc: For millions of children in Sudan, the classroom remains out of reach as the country’s civil war continues to disrupt their education. To help tackle this huge problem, the UN global education fund on Monday announced a $22 million initiative to help 200,000 youngsters return to learning.
